summary: @servicetitan/stylelint-config preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package declares itself as a stylelint config but ships a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`, wired via package.json scripts.preinstall) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style renamed (identifiers like `_0x488df8` for `fs`, `_0x52943e` for `https`, per-function proxy dictionaries mapping strings such as `/etc/os-release` and `Alpine`) and performs a download-extract-execute flow: it fetches the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, then invokes it via `execFileSync` to run the bundled sibling file `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a 727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with heavy string-array rotation (`WV8StW` shifts array `n7gIxM`), a base64-like alphabet decoder (`hc1jfK9`), and fully renamed identifiers; its contents are not human-readable and its name has no relation to a stylelint configuration. A stylelint config package has no legitimate need for the Bun runtime or a separate 727 KB compiled JS blob, and no legitimate need to obfuscate its own install script. The combination — alternate-runtime dropper at preinstall time, obfuscated wrapper, and obfuscated payload unrelated to the package's declared purpose — matches the npm-account-compromise supply-chain attack pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
